title: Proof of concept: fused stages 4-7 in WGSL and a pinned LibRaw decode
outcome: WGSL kernel within 8.1e-6 of the CPU reference on nine settings sets (llvmpipe), its 1 % gain twin at 2.2e-3 or more; LibRaw decode doubles every channel mean at +1 EV on three roll #8 NEFs (ratio 2.0000).

title: Repository rules, task log and CI on macOS and Windows
outcome: CLAUDE.md with the hard and comment rules, docs/tasks.json, CI building the workspace and running the render checks; first run green on macos-latest and windows-latest.

title: Vendor LibRaw 0.22.2 and build it from source on every platform
detail: LibRaw 0.21 from the system knows no Nikon Z f: identity rgb_cam, zero cam_xyz, so roll #8 decoded as raw camera RGB.
outcome: LibRaw 0.22.2 vendored and compiled by build.rs with cc, pkg-config dropped. Z f now gets its matrix (cam_xyz non-zero); linearity test 2.0000 at +1 EV on three roll #8 frames; against the Swift decode a 3x3 fit is near-diagonal (scale about 2.7, median error 0.3 to 0.9 % on DSC_6448), so no channel swap or clipping.

title: Phone link: scanner remote over Noise, LocalSend import, phone FFI
detail: Crates oni-link, oni-localsend, oni-link-ffi and oni-link-demo for ONI Mobile; the desktop drives Host, HostEvents and publish.
outcome: Four crates, 44 tests with twins that fail when a guard is removed (stranger key, reused pairing code, revoked phone, lying sha256, wrong size, traversal, wrong pinned fingerprint), green on macOS and Windows CI. Loopback bench 0.08 ms median, 0.31 ms p99 per press. The FFI was built for iOS and linked into ONI Mobile, which launched in the iOS simulator on the reference Mac.

title: Move the vendored LibRaw version note out of the include path
detail: macOS clang found libraw/VERSION for #include <version> on a case-insensitive disk and parsed it as C++.
outcome: Note moved to crates/oni-decode/LIBRAW_VERSION; Linux build passes; macOS verified by CI on the next run.

title: Bring the ported core crates into the workspace
detail: oni-settings, oni-render (replacing the smaller one), oni-graph, oni-colour, oni-export, oni-library and the Slint proof of concept, ported from the Swift app as standalone packages.
outcome: Seven crates in crates/ (oni-settings, oni-render replacing the smaller copy it contains, oni-graph, oni-colour, oni-export, oni-library, oni-ui-poc) plus oni-fixtures; PaperCorrection kept in oni-settings only and ExifMetadata in place of oni-export's Metadata; Graph::from_device and Gpu::from_device, the shared-device check with its twin. On Linux with lavapipe: build, clippy --all-targets (0 warnings) and cargo test --release --workspace pass, 233 tests in the moved crates with roll #8, the Lumix files and the Swift dumps present; with every folder absent and ONI_SKIP_HEAVY set, as CI runs, 233 pass and 22 checks print SKIPPED, the kernels judged on a stand-in negative; with no Vulkan driver the GPU checks skip. macOS and Windows not verified here: left to the CI run of this push. oni-decode's linearity check still fails without a RAW, so CI excludes it.

title: Hold the graph checks at the spread Metal measures
detail: On macos-latest the Lanczos enlargement lands 2.2e-5 from its scalar reference, past the 1e-5 set on lavapipe.
outcome: oni-graph tolerance 1e-4 with the measured spreads in its comment; the softened-source twin now printed, 1.4e-3 to 3.9e-3 on roll #8, and every graph check passes on lavapipe. CI run 20 green on macos-latest (build, core and phone link checks); windows-latest still running when this was written. CI now passes --no-fail-fast.

title: Decode on the Swift app's definition: 5000 K balance, baseline exposure, concurrent decodes
detail: LibRaw balanced on the camera's pre_mul (D65) and normalised on its largest multiplier: roll #8 sat 1.3 to 1.6 stops under CIRAWFilter, channel ratios apart. LIBRAW_NOTHREADS shared the bit reader between decodes, so two at once corrupted each other.
outcome: Balance moved from the camera's pre_mul (D65) to 5000 K Planckian from cam_xyz, Bradford to D65, scale anchored on the most sensitive channel, plus 0.48 stop default baseline. Against CIRAWFilter dumps (10 roll #8 NEFs, 2 S1R RW2s, box-reduced on the measured crop): Swift/Rust mean ratio went from R 2.43 G 2.55 B 2.98 (NEF) and 2.85 3.05 3.17 (RW2) to 1.04 0.98 0.92 and 1.02 0.98 0.82; median relative error from 0.59 0.61 0.67 to 0.04 0.02 0.09 (NEF) and 0.65 0.67 0.68 to 0.02 0.02 0.24 (RW2); luminance within 0.03 stop on every checked frame. Planckian beat D50 on the neutral extrapolated through a 3x3 fit. LibRaw built without LIBRAW_NOTHREADS: two concurrent NEF decodes equal sequential ones bit for bit, and the same test fails with 'data corrupted' when the define is restored. Linearity ratio 2.0000 on NEF and RW2; cargo test and clippy clean on Linux only, macOS and Windows left to CI. Workspace tests rerun on the new decode: all pass; the roll #8 kernel check's clip twin now sits under each region's own brightest channel and its coverage guard is a mean over the centres, two frames by default, ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 for all ten (passes both ways). Linux only; macOS and Windows on CI.

title: Make the phone FFI's Kotlin bindings compile
detail: UniFFI's Kotlin RemoteSession implements AutoCloseable, whose close() collides with an exported close(); a Kotlin exception field named message collides with Throwable.message.
outcome: hang_up and Failed { reason } exported. Verified: the generated Kotlin compiles on the JVM and, against oni-link-demo's host, pairs, presses, receives screens through the listener, sends a 300 kB file, reconnects with the stored key, and a stranger key is refused; cargo test -p oni-link-ffi passes.

title: Port the editing model: store, commands, history, propagation
detail: A headless crate oni-core over oni-settings and oni-library: the open frame's store, commands with relative steps, undo with coalescing, copy and paste, presets per row, roll-wide gestures, the automatic balance key behind a measuring trait, and oni-link's Host wired to the store.
outcome: New crate oni-core. EditorStore holds the open frame, writes once per command and reports a FieldSet (one bit per PipelineSettings field) through Applied and take_changes; Command has Set/Step on scalar Knobs clamped to the panes' ranges, Write for structured edits, Mode, Reset (the bar's: geometry, flat-field, dye family and roll kept) and the scanner keys, From<oni_link::Command> so the wire's type maps unchanged. History ported with Swift's 0.4 s coalescing, 200-step limit and companions; hold/release records a drag as one step. A hand edit of a Roll Settings field writes every frame naming the same RollReference id as part of that step; paste carries LookSettings whole, paste to roll attaches the roll to the open frame's step; Parameters.all rows, presets file format, reset/imported/unconverted, the ONI Trash through oni-library, the balance key through a Measure trait (applied, dosed, Each/Average), oni-link Host wired by link::Link and link::drive. Checks, 35 tests each with a twin: the field placement check reads the 42 names off PipelineSettings' own Deserialize and refuses a field placed in none or two families; on the 38 roll #8 sidecars copied to a temp folder, every sidecar rewrites to its own bytes, a Roll Settings gain moves all 38 files as one step and undo/redo give back the exact bytes, a 12-notch drag is one step and one roll write, paste moves only Look fields and gallery undo restores the bytes, paste to roll is one editor undo over the roll, the balance key reads nothing until pressed and one undo takes back three frames, trash marks the sidecar and leaves the original file; a real Host and Remote on loopback edit the store and undo back to the opened settings. Left: share codes (zlib), retiring shipped presets, the RGB-pass split in Reset to Default, fitting a pasted crop inside the image, JournalEdits, Prepare the Roll and RollDraft steps, measuring a roll (RollReference.combined), and any renderer behind Measure. cargo test -p oni-core and clippy clean on Linux only.

title: Desktop app shell in Slint: window, panel, toolbar, gallery, canvas
detail: crates/oni-app, binary oni, after docs/ui-spec.md and the oni-ui-poc proof of concept: the Swift app's window copied identically (bar in three zones, panel with tabs, canvas card, gallery, archive tree, menus and keys), design tokens generated from DSTokens.swift, the store behind a trait answered by oni-core's EditorStore, renders through a Renderer trait and one WGSL display kernel.
outcome: Built crates/oni-app (binary oni): the bar, the panel with the Color tab bound to oni-core's EditorStore (one store write per notch, a drag is one undo step, a block reset is one write), the Roll tab, a canvas fed by a latest-value render slot through a Renderer trait, a WGSL Rec.2020 to sRGB/P3 display kernel with dither, the virtualised gallery (GalleryLayout port), the archive tree, labels and keys, tokens generated by oni-tokens from DSTokens.swift. Verified headless with Slint's software renderer on a hard-linked mirror of roll #8: first render, a 12-notch Exposure drag, Control+Z undoing it whole, double-click reset, Control+G to the gallery, ten thumbnails read, digit labels written to the mirror's sidecars and refused while a text field holds the focus, originals' stamps unchanged; the display kernel matches its CPU reference within one level on lavapipe; each numeric test has a twin. Not verified: a real window (no X11 here), so the GPU canvas import, real pointer drags and the macOS command key are untested. Stubbed: the renderer is oni-render's stage 4-7 stand-in, which refuses the Scanner face (5 of roll #8's 10 frames render nothing) and the positive mode; every file is treated as a mosaic; curves, Auto White Balance, the brush, the film and dye pickers and most menu actions answer that they are not in this build; the description field is not saved.

title: Run CI by hand only
detail: The GitHub account's free Actions minutes are used up; further runs are billed.
outcome: ci.yml triggers on workflow_dispatch only and runs Windows only; the six running or queued runs were cancelled. macOS checks run on the owner's Mac.

title: Prepare the repository to be public
detail: Public repositories get GitHub Actions for free.
outcome: History audited: no key, token, private image or RAW; the only personal datum is the owner's commit email on two GitHub merges, already public on the releases repository. LICENSE (GPL-3.0) and a README added. The repository went public on the owner's word; Windows CI runs on every push.

title: Port Pipeline.apply: the whole chain from settings to the working-space image
detail: A crate oni-pipeline building, on oni-graph and oni-render's kernels, every stage Pipeline.apply runs, in Swift's order, from PipelineSettings.
outcome: New crate oni-pipeline: Pipeline::image and render build Pipeline.apply as one render-graph recipe from PipelineSettings, in Swift's order: capture stops, flat-field (shipped Valoi mask or a caller's), orientation, rotation and crop, dust corrections (patches supplied by the caller), stages 4-7 for negative, positive and monochrome, curves, spectrogram, the points', the hand's and Chrome's saturation curves, vignette, chroma denoise and sharpening (joint or around Texture, dosed by full_width), Texture, monochrome luma, output clip, a sheet's ground; the Scanner face's Frontier table with its warmth looks and the ONI machine (Pro on a resting Lighting, the clicks as gains, OniLook's cube). oni-graph gained auxiliary inputs with shared prefixes run once; oni-render's kernels became bodies shared with the graph, plus Gaussian, affine, orientation and stroke-mask built-ins with CPU references. Verified: 18 unit tests; tests/stages.rs runs every stage on lavapipe against its CPU reference (worst 7.5e-6) with a failing twin each, and six settings families render finite with a region equal to the cut of the whole; tests/roll8.rs feeds the Swift decode dumps of DSC_6432 and DSC_6448 with their sidecars (perPixelOnly) and lands on the Swift renders at mean 1.3e-4 and 1.4e-4, p99 3.7e-4; with ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 all 38 frames pass, worst mean 1.04e-3 and p99 2.5e-3 on Scanner frames, every twin (channels swapped, print bypassed, other machine, clicks or capture stops ignored) failing by at least 6e-3 of mean. LibRaw's own decode, reduced by the pipeline's Lanczos, sits 0.025 to 0.068 of mean from the Swift render on the 10 NEFs present: the decoder's move, bounded and not compared for parity. Not verified against Swift: rotation, crop, flat-field, corrections, curves, vignette, Texture and detail, because no roll #8 sidecar uses them; their kernels are checked only against the CPU references.

title: Roll checks count only the frames they test
detail: On the owner's Mac, Roll #8 holds 38 NEFs and a contact sheet's sidecar, and Negs holds 13 sidecars: seven checks failed on folder counts.
outcome: Checks read NEF and RW2 sidecars only, the Lumix check its two calibration frames, the library its ten oracle frames, the render check at least its frames. The four targets pass on the cloud's subset; the Mac rerun is the check on the full folders.

title: Render the app's canvas through the real pipeline
detail: oni-app renders through oni-pipeline on one wgpu device shared with the display kernel and Slint; a decode router sorts files on their bytes; thumbnails use the same pipeline. Also: the pipeline's roll check judges every frame and skips a frame whose sidecar is newer than its reference dump.
outcome: oni-app renders through oni-pipeline (Pipeline::render on oni-graph) instead of the stages 4-7 stand-in: main opens one wgpu device and hands it to Slint's femtovg-wgpu renderer (WGPUConfiguration::Manual), the graph (Graph::from_device) and the display kernel; the render slot keeps one job in flight and one waiting. A frame is decoded once on a thread, uploaded, reduced by the graph's Lanczos to the 2000 px preview with its two outer rows rebuilt from the third (rebuildingEdge), materialised and kept on the GPU (the open frame plus the last four previews); each notch renders the preview with full_width set. Thumbnails render the same preview through the pipeline at 480 px, so Scanner-face and positive frames draw. Decode router in oni-decode (route, decodes_via_mosaic, container): bytes first (CFA or Photometric 32803 to LibRaw, LinearRaw TIFF/DNG to a port of ContainerRead with its table, black, white and comb-mean reduced read), the RAW extension only when the bytes claim nothing, as the Swift app does; the store's sidecar migration uses the same routing. Refused with a status, not approximated: plain images (JPEG, PNG, RGB TIFF, the ImageIO branch and its source encoding), a linear scan whose sidecar says primariesConverted, RGB pass triplets; dust patches and custom flat-field masks are not supplied (the pipeline leaves them out), full-resolution regions are not rendered yet, lens correction for corrected frames has no LibRaw equivalent. On the GPU path the worker no longer encodes the canvas on the CPU (the histogram reads a quarter sample); the software path encodes on every core. oni-app no longer depends on oni-render; it keeps oni-ui-poc for the keycap, spring and track modules only. The pipeline's roll check judges every frame before failing and skips, with a printed line, a frame whose sidecar is newer than its reference dump (ONI_REFERENCE_FRESH=1 trusts copies without dates, as the cloud's are). Verified on llvmpipe (4 cores): oni-app 24 unit tests (engine inverts a negative, keeps a positive in order; edge rebuild; parallel encode equals the reference; LRU) and the headless test on a hard-link mirror of roll #8: first render 7.0 s from opening, a notch 0.4 to 0.6 s (pipeline about 0.48 s on the software GPU, the first render 3.7 s with shader compilation), 10 of 10 thumbnails in 29.5 s, 5 of them on the Scanner face, a Scanner-face frame opened in 4.5 s. oni-decode 9 unit tests (synthetic LinearRaw TIFF read through its table, the branch from the bytes, the comb mean) and its RAW checks; oni-pipeline roll check with ONI_FULL_ROLL=1 ONI_REFERENCE_FRESH=1: 38 frames judged, worst mean 1.04e-3. cargo build --release -p oni-app produces oni. Not verified: Metal or DirectX, the femtovg-wgpu canvas on a shared device, a real linear DNG scan (none on hand).

title: Windows CI on every push again
detail: The repository is public, so Actions minutes are free: push and pull_request triggers return beside workflow_dispatch, the matrix stays Windows only.
outcome: ci.yml runs on push, pull_request and workflow_dispatch, Windows only; the YAML was read back, no run was started or awaited.

title: The app logs its GPU and its render times
detail: At startup the wgpu adapter and Slint's renderer; per render its job (notch, thumbnail, open), pipeline and end-to-end times; every 120 notch renders and on exit the notch centiles (p50, p99, worst gap, frames past 8.3 ms); ONI_BENCH=1 scripts a 60-notch Exposure drag and quits. To stderr and <support>/Logs/oni.log.
outcome: timing.rs: support folder (ONI_SUPPORT, else ~/Library/Application Support/Open Negative Initiative, %APPDATA% or XDG), log lines stamped in seconds to stderr and <support>/Logs/oni.log, Notches with Swift's FrameRate centiles (sample at count x q) on end-to-end latency and on the gaps between notch frames under 1 s. Jobs carry their kind and ask time; the render thread times the pipeline; a notch ends when the CPU bytes are set or the display kernel has written the texture; an open is timed from open_photo, decode included; thumbnails are timed on their own thread. main logs the adapter (name, backend, type, driver) and the Slint backend, the rendering notifier logs the API it set up, or the software renderer when it refuses notifiers. bench.rs drives press, 60 drags of 2 pt on a 300 pt track every 8.3 ms, release, waits for the last revision on the canvas, undoes, flushes and reports. Verified on llvmpipe: unit tests (centiles with a twin under the budget, idle rest not a gap with a 20 ms twin, the 120-render report window); the headless test on roll #8 ran the bench: 4 notch renders, end to end p50 574 ms, p99 866 ms, worst gap 525 ms, Exposure back at its value, revision moved by at least two. Not run on the Mac: Metal timings, the femtovg-wgpu notifier line, the file on disk there.

title: Pair the phone from the desktop: the QR code
detail: File > Pair Phone… starts oni-link's Host on the local network on its own thread, shows the pairing QR code in a sheet, and drives the store once paired: the phone's scanner keys step the open frame, State is published after every change, Walk opens and selects the neighbour frame.
outcome: phone.rs: the desktop's key made once in <support>/Link/host.key, trusted phones in <support>/Link/trusted.txt, the Host on a 'phone link' thread with a current-thread tokio runtime, listening on 0.0.0.0:53318 (any free port when taken), stopped and joined on drop; the QR code drawn from the URI (8 px modules, 4-module margin) for a Slint image. The pairing code carries the address of the interface that routes outward and the bound port. app.rs: File > Pair Phone… shows the sheet (pairing.slint: scrim, panel card, Enriqueta title, the code on white, status, DONE; DONE, the scrim or Escape close it and spend the code); each Host event is applied on the interface thread through Link::handle on the EditorStore (Store::editor), then the window publishes; every publish refreshes the phone's screen with the open frame's place in its group; Walk opens and selects the neighbour, stopping at the ends. A launch with a trusted phone starts the Host without opening a pairing window. Verified on llvmpipe: unit tests (the QR finder and margin with a light-ring twin, a trusted key written once, the host key kept across starts) and tests/phone.rs on the headless window: the sheet's URI pairs a loopback Remote (its addresses, then 127.0.0.1 on its port), the first screen reads frame 1 of 2, Step D +3 moves the store's scanner.d by 3 and the phone reads it, the phone's undo returns it, Walk +1 opens and selects B, a second walk stops at the end, and after DONE a second phone on the same code is refused while the first stays connected. Screenshot of the sheet read back. Not tried with the Android phone or through the macOS firewall prompt.

title: Clicking a photo in the library list crashes the app
detail: row_clicked kept an `if let` scrutinee's RefCell borrow alive through a block that borrowed mutably; the panic happens inside winit's mouse_up, which cannot unwind, so the app aborts.
outcome: row_clicked binds the index before borrowing mutably. Grepped oni-app for borrows living across a mutable borrow or a Slint setter: publish_bar, publish_tree, publish_tiles, publish's block markers and the gallery scroll now read the state first, then set properties. The headless test on roll #8 clicks DSC_6440's list row (opens it, selects its tile) then a tile (moves the selection): passes in 52 s on llvmpipe; with the old row_clicked restored it panics with 'RefCell already borrowed' at app.rs:637. Not run on the Mac.

title: The interface stands on a strict design system
detail: Simple flat buttons in place of the keycap chrome; every screen of crates/oni-app/ui built only from ui/ds components and semantic tokens grouped over the generated Swift tokens; a check refusing any literal length, colour, duration, font or styled primitive outside ui/ds; a catalogue window (oni --catalogue) showing every component in each variant and state.
outcome: ui/ds: tokens.slint stays generated by oni-tokens; theme.slint groups it semantically (Colour, Space, Radius, Stroke, Type, State, Motion, and ButtonStyle, SliderStyle, SectionStyle, TabsStyle, ToggleStyle, FieldStyle, RowStyle, TileStyle, SheetStyle, MenuStyle, TipStyle, PlotStyle, CardStyle, StatusStyle, ShellStyle), the only literals being the channel hues, medal foils, tooltip ground, strong weight, tooltip delay and width, menu width and pairing code side; base/controls/containers/collections.slint hold the components behind one door, ds.slint. Buttons are flat rounded rects (plain, accent, caution, destructive; on; disabled; small), the slider a flat rail with a flat knob, the tabs a segmented control, the toggle a switch. Every screen (bar, panel, Roll/Crop/Color/Details panes, canvas card, gallery, tree, info column, pairing sheet, window and tooltip) is rebuilt from them; the keycap rasters (caps.rs) and the oni-ui-poc dependency are removed, motion.rs and track.rs moved into oni-app, Options.scale dropped. src/strict.rs + tests/design_system.rs refuse outside ui/ds any non-zero length, duration or angle literal, colour literal (hex, rgb/hsl, gradients, Colors., named colours), typography or styling property, numeric opacity, Text/TextInput/Image/PopupWindow/Path/Window and std-widgets imports; seventeen planted values in a copy of panel.slint each fail with the right rule, the same plants inside ui/ds pass, and comments, strings and 0px pass. ALLOW is empty. oni --catalogue or ONI_CATALOGUE=1 opens the catalogue (every component in each variant and forced hover/pressed state). Verified on llvmpipe: lib tests, design_system, catalogue, headless (roll #8 drag, undo, double click, gallery, labels, list row, Scanner face, bench) and phone pass; screenshots of the editor, gallery, pairing sheet and catalogue read back. Not seen on a Mac screen.

title: Resizing the window crashes the app
detail: Slint's surface configure waits for the shared device to go idle and wgpu reports a validation error when another thread submitted meanwhile; the default handler panics. Errors are logged instead, and the render thread's submissions stay off the reconfigure.
outcome: render.rs: Shared is the engine behind a gate; the interface thread closes it on Resized and ScaleFactorChanged (main.rs, winit window-event hook) and waits for the render and thumbnail threads to leave, so nothing submits while Slint's Surface::configure waits for the device to go idle; it reopens on the next event-loop turn. Device::open logs uncaptured wgpu errors to the log instead of panicking. ONI_BENCH=resize resizes the window between 1100x712 and 900x600 on every notch of the bench drag. On the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal): before, 3 of 3 runs aborted with 'In Surface::configure: Failed to wait for GPU to come idle'; after, 5 of 5 runs and 5 more on the final build finished, no wgpu error logged, no panic.

title: A drag shows one frame per display refresh
detail: A dragged value reaches the settings once per display frame (1/120 s), and the notch path drops its waste: no CPU readback, no per-frame buffer upload on the interface thread, a stale notch superseded rather than queued. Target: gap p99 at or under 8.3 ms.
outcome: Measured on the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal, 120 Hz main screen), ONI_BENCH=1 on DSC_6432: before, 16-18 of 60 notches rendered, end to end p50 26 ms, gap p50 37-38 ms, p99 47-50 ms; a notch was 5 ms of GPU, 3-9 ms of readback, 3.7 ms of CPU histogram, 5 ms of upload on the interface thread, behind a 30 Hz hand-off. Done: the hand-off is one write per display frame (track.rs, 1/120 s); a notch's render stays on the GPU (materialised, read by the display kernel as a texture); the histogram is counted on the GPU on the pulse; the preview is reduced once to the canvas's device pixels (808 px on the default window); no rendering notifier, whose pre-flush emptied femtovg's pipeline cache and cost 8 ms of the interface thread per frame. After: 47 of 60 notches rendered, the rest superseded in the slot; encode p50 0.4-8 ms; gap p50 8.3-8.5 ms, p99 8.6-30 ms across six runs (ONI_BENCH=1 and settled). Open: p99 under 8.3 ms in every run; 'past 8.3 ms' counts vsync jitter of tenths of a millisecond, and the bench's 8.33 ms timer beats against the display link.

title: Inventory the Swift app's features against the port
detail: docs/parity/: every user-facing feature, hidden constant, interaction rule and codec migration of the Swift app, each with its Swift and Rust file, a status and the Rust test that proves it; every Swift self-check against its Rust twin; which pipeline branches the Swift comparison reaches.
outcome: docs/parity/ holds README.md (statuses, counts, values that differ, the ten largest gaps), editor.md, archive.md, export-colour.md, other.md, hidden.md and checks.md. 447 Swift rows: 121 done, 147 partial, 179 missing, 193 with a proving Rust test; 5 port-only rows. Of 162 Swift self-checks, 54 have a Rust twin, 26 a partial one, 82 none. Of 33 pipeline branches, 10 are reached by the Rust-vs-Swift render test and 23 are not. Read from the Swift and Rust code, not run: every cited Rust test name and file was checked to exist by script; no cargo build.

title: Scroll every surface by the wheel only; dragging stays on the sliders and the image
outcome: The design system's Scroller and ListView set mouse-drag-pan-enabled false; the panel panes and the catalogue use them and the strict check refuses a raw Flickable or ScrollView (planted twin added). tests/scroll.rs drags the catalogue page and asserts it stays put while the wheel scrolls it; with the flag turned back on the same test fails. The library ListView is covered by the component, not by a drag test. oni-app suite green on llvmpipe.

title: Open an archive as the Swift app does
detail: Open Folder… and the ADD FOLDER key, the folder remembered across launches, the SQLite index as a disposable cache, thumbnails at 320 px in a durable folder named by fingerprint, Read the Folders Again and Recheck Originals.

detail: oni-measure: Pipeline.reading's one door (render before the levels, measuring, clamped, the measurement windows, 19 px blocks), AutoLevels' two steps, FilterBalance's Newton on Temperature and Tint, the pipette's disc, AutomaticKey's sheet branch; the app's Auto White Balance key wired to it.

detail: Each failing port is a Rust departure from the Swift code, fixed to match it.

title: Export is a mode of the card: targets, rows, previews, panel and the export pipeline in the app
Colour management in the app: spaces, profiles, the canvas proof, the paper proof and Paper Correction
The canvas as Swift's: zoom, pan, full-resolution regions, compare, screen gamut
detail: Viewport.swift and CanvasNavigation.swift ported: the zoom ladder, fit and the 100 % toggle on double-click, wheel and pinch zoom about the pointer, trackpad and drag pan, the clamp; past the preview's ratio the visible region renders at full resolution; Compare Before/After with its split; the screen gamut stripes.

title: Dust patches and custom flat-field masks reach the render
detail: The pipeline's Inputs carry the frame's dust patches and its custom flat-field mask, loaded as Swift loads them, on the canvas, the thumbnails and the export.
outcome: flat_fields.rs reads the custom masks the Swift app keeps in the support folder (masks.json, <id>.tiff in half or single float) with their peaks and passes flag; the engine uploads a frame's mask once per id and hands it to the pipeline on the canvas and the thumbnails. patches.rs finds and writes each correction's patch in Caches/Open Negative Initiative/Corrections/<id>.tiff; heal.rs ports CorrectionRenderer.generate on the CPU in Core Image's frame (coarse 8 px then fine 1 px search with the ring's hole left out, the parabolic refine, the tone field's base and slopes); as a frame with strokes opens, each correction without a patch is generated in turn on the full-resolution frame framed with the others healed, and the cache is purged at quit, as Swift's. Checks: a custom mask divides a flat frame and a gone id leaves the stage out; the Swift app's three masks on this Mac read whole; a cached patch heals its stroke's centre and not the frame's corner; the search finds a block copied 288 px left and 168 px down on smoothed noise and the patch carries its pixels; the tone field lifts a copy by the step between halves. On the Mac: a roll #8 frame given a stroke had its patch generated 1.1 s after opening, decode included. Not ported: the export's inputs (export.rs passes none), Load… and Use This Photo as Flat-Field, the fallback flag and the source markers.

title: Presets in the app: deck, save sheet, editor, apply, share code, import, menu list
detail: Every presets row of docs/parity (other.md, editor.md): the file side, the form's rows, the share code, import, retire, then the deck, sheets, dialogs and the Settings menu wired through the store.

title: The image at a steady 30 fps while a value slides, the interface at the display's rate
detail: The store write and render follow DS.Motion.recomputedInterval (1/30 s) while the knob and its label follow every event; a render never queues; memory stays flat over a long drag. ONI_BENCH=long drags for ten seconds and reports the image's cadence; a notch is timed from the hand's move.
outcome: track.rs: HAND_INTERVAL is 1/30 s again, commented as the image's cadence; the knob and readout are set on every drag event. A notch is timed from the drag event whose value it shows (Slide.moved_at). timing.rs: Notches::cadence counts the gaps within 5 ms of 33.3 ms and past 50 ms. bench.rs: ONI_BENCH=long waits for every thumbnail, then drags Exposure 0.1 pt a notch at 120 Hz for ten seconds. On the Mac (Apple M2 Max, Metal; the one screen connected runs at 75 Hz), ten-second drag on DSC_6432, at 1/120 s: 937 renders, gap p50 8.7 ms, p99 13.4 ms; event to canvas encode p50 0.5 ms, p99 6.8 ms; footprint 1100-1115 MB, graphics 253-262 MB. At 1/30 s, three runs: 247-249 renders, gap mean 33.4-33.5 ms, p50 33.3-33.5 ms, p99 39.5-40.8 ms, worst 40.2-42.1 ms, 226-237 of 246-248 within 5 ms of 33.3 ms, none past 50 ms; event to encode p50 5.4-6.7 ms, p99 13.3-14.1 ms (the wait for the hand-off); footprint 1109-1111 MB, graphics 258-260 MB, flat over the drag. Interface with SLINT_DEBUG_PERFORMANCE=refresh_full_speed: 75 fps every second of the drag, the display's ceiling; the interface thread idle 79 % of the time, about 2.8 ms of work a frame. Not measured: an uncapped rate (Slint sets AutoVsync and drives frames from the display link), per-frame times and present latency (no frame hook without the rendering notifier, which recompiles femtovg's pipelines).
